subject: physics
question_text: Define strain and explain the types of strain.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.100). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: strain = change in dimension per unit original dimension, dimensionless; the three types are longitudinal (Δl/l), volume/bulk (ΔV/V) and shearing (angle of shear θ).

steps.label: Strain — the definition
lines: A deforming force changes the size or

It is a ratio, so it has no unit and
steps.margin_note: The words "per unit original dimension" earn this mark, not the symbol alone.
steps.why: Strain is defined as a ratio of two similar quantities so that the same formula describes a change in length, in volume or in shape, whatever the size of the body.
common_mistakes: Giving strain a unit such as metre. It is a ratio of two lengths or volumes, so it has none.
Defining strain only for length and leaving out volume and shape changes.
steps.memory_tip: Strain is a ratio, so it never carries a unit.

steps.label: Longitudinal strain
lines: along the length of a body changes its
where Δl is the change in length and l
steps.margin_note: Name the type and give the ratio: change in length over original length.
steps.why: Longitudinal strain is the one used with Young's modulus, so writing it in change-over-original form here is what a later numerical reuses directly.
common_mistakes: Writing l/Δl upside down. The change goes on top, the original length on the bottom.
Naming the type without giving its ratio.
steps.memory_tip: Longitudinal strain is Δl over l: the change over the original length.

steps.label: Volume strain
lines: strain. When a body under uniform
pressure changes its volume but not
where ΔV is the change in volume and V
steps.margin_note: The words "shape stays the same" separate this from shearing strain.
steps.why: Volume strain pairs with the bulk modulus B = P/(ΔV/V), so writing it as change over original volume here is what makes that later formula legible.
common_mistakes: Saying the shape also changes. Under uniform pressure only the volume changes.
Writing ΔV/ΔP in place of ΔV/V.
steps.memory_tip: Volume strain is ΔV over V: the change over the original volume.

steps.label: Shearing strain
lines: displaces one face of a body relative
to the fixed opposite face. The
steps.margin_note: Naming this as an angle θ, not a length, earns this mark.
steps.why: The two faces stay the same distance apart everywhere, so the ratio of the tangential displacement to that distance is a single number, and geometrically it equals the angle the body has sheared through.
common_mistakes: Giving shearing strain a length instead of an angle.
Confusing it with longitudinal strain, which changes a length, not a shape.
steps.memory_tip: Shearing strain is the angle of shear θ: a sideways push tilts the body.

insider_note: Three of the four marks are the three types of strain. A definition with only two types still loses a mark.
